A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Edit-aware RAW Reconstruction, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material. Content can be matched across layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, target-edit fine-tuning, and ablations, including Tables 2-4 and S1-S4.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a user study, image-specific editing experiments, NUS camera evaluations, and loss-weight sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The four-module sampled ISP, reconstruction objectives, and target-edit fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged in Equations (1)-(11) and (S1)-(S3). The additional sampling-threshold disclosure does not establish an actual algorithm revision.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates the Samsung S24 Ultra dataset. v2 additionally evaluates NUS data from Samsung NX2000, Olympus E-PL6, and Sony SLT-A57 cameras in Section S4. Section 4.4 also adds manual, image-specific edits, substantially broadening camera coverage and editing scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CAM, RAW Diffusion, UNet, and the CIE XYZ Net cyclic-loss comparison. The latter moves from Table S4 to S6. New experiments reuse existing comparison methods without introducing a new competing reconstruction method.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a blind forced-choice study with 25 users judging 20 images for three methods, yielding 1,500 responses. Additional protocols cover manual edits on 50 challenging images, NUS evaluation following the CAM protocol with two specified edits, and a lambda sweep over 1, 2, 4, and 8. Existing smartphone splits and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table S5 adds loss-weight sensitivity analysis for CAM and RAW Diffusion, while Section 4.4 tests robustness to image-specific edits. These extend the retained component, sampling-range, cyclic-loss, dehazing, and local-tone-mapping analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new participant counts describe evaluation design; preference percentages and hyperparameter sweeps do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All retained quantitative table entries are unchanged, including v1 Table S4 matched to v2 Table S6. New outcomes include 83% overall user preference, manual-edit results such as CAM's 22.11 dB baseline versus 24.36 dB with edit-aware loss, and NUS and lambda-sweep scores. NUS results also show reduced RAW PSNR and a Sony Edit B PSNR tie at 33.26 dB. These are additional experiments, not improvements to previously reported scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and assumptions, including normalized, demosaiced, denoised three-channel RAW inputs, are retained. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a plug-and-play edit-aware loss, improved edited-sRGB fidelity with reported gains up to 1.5-2 dB, and target-edit fine-tuning for metadata-assisted reconstruction. The added experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly clarifies independence from the actual capture and inference ISPs, interprets the new results as supporting image-specific editing and limited lambda sensitivity, and identifies failures under extreme low light or unfamiliar illumination such as green LEDs. These concrete failure conditions replace v1's closing future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v2 quantifies training overhead at approximately 15% and newly specifies an ASN-neighborhood threshold of L1 <= 0.05. v1 mentions both overhead and neighborhood restriction without these values. The new L1 specification conflicts with the Euclidean wording retained in Section 3.2, leaving the precise norm ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cheng, Prasad, and Brown's 2014 work as the NUS dataset reference. Existing research positioning against RAW-fidelity objectives and unedited cyclic consistency remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Local rewrites clarify ISP access and shorten related work. v2 adds Sections 4.3, 4.4, and supplementary Section S4, renumbers additional ablations to S5, and revises the conclusion. The abstract, overall narrative, and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, S4, and S5 and renumbers the existing cyclic-loss table to S6. Figures 3 and 4 each shrink from six examples to four; the two displaced RAW Diffusion examples move into Figure S2, replacing two previous examples. Figure 5 moves from page 8 to page 7. The overall visual format and core diagrams remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the paper's practical editing claims: NUS experiments extend the single-camera evidence, the blind user study directly tests perceptual matching, and manual image-specific edits address the restriction to fixed edit recipes. Failure conditions and quantified training overhead also improve transparency. These gains address important evidentiary gaps in v1, despite limited uncertainty reporting and the inconsistent white-balance norm specification.
